headline: GOLD SURGES 4% TO $3,672 AS AI SELLOFF FADES — Barrick +6.7%, Newmont +6.4%, AngloGold +7.8%, Kinross +6% in Biggest Miner Rally of 2026 Correction
snippet: Gold surged 4% to $3,672 per ounce by mid-US session on November 23 as forced selling tied to the AI tech unwind faded and the dollar rally stalled, with Barrick Mining gaining 6.7%, Newmont advancing 6.4%, AngloGold Ashanti rising 7.8%, and Kinross climbing 6% — the largest single-session recovery for gold miners since the correction began. The bounce follows gold's worst week of 2026, a 9% decline driven by AI-linked margin calls and aggressive Fed hike pricing. Gold remains down 32% from its January $5,405 record high, leaving major miners at valuations last seen in 2022.

headline: CAMECO JUMPS 7.4% AS JENSEN HUANG CONFIRMED RETURNING TO NVIDIA — Uranium Equities Snap Losing Streak as AI Demand Thesis Reactivates
snippet: Cameco (NYSE: CCJ) gained 7.4% in New York on November 23 as uranium equities snapped a week-long losing streak after news confirmed Jensen Huang would return as Nvidia's CEO — reviving hopes that datacenter AI infrastructure spending would recover its trajectory and restore near-term uranium demand. Northern Miner's analysis notes the rally is sentiment-driven and that the uranium equity-to-commodity disconnect remains extreme: Cameco's realized price was approximately $65.8/lb in Q3 2026 against a spot price near $90/lb, while the URNM ETF is down 31% year-to-date.

headline: TSX FUTURES JUMP 3.5% AS GOLD BOUNCES AND NVIDIA SENTIMENT REVERSES — Canadian Mining Stocks Join Global Relief Rally
snippet: Canadian equity futures climbed 3.5% on November 23 as a recovery in gold prices and reversal of Nvidia-linked selling pressure lifted the TSX, which carries significant weighting in precious metals, uranium, and base metals equities. For TSX-V investors, the session marks the first meaningful relief from a correction that has pushed many junior gold explorers to multi-year lows. Wednesday's US CPI print remains the critical near-term test for whether the bounce has legs or represents a dead-cat move in a deteriorating macro environment.

headline: GOLD TERRA CONFIRMS GOLD IN 30-YEAR DORMANT CON MINE TAILINGS — Yellowknife Peak 3.75 g/t Au; First 6-Hole Sonic Program Opens New NWT Resource
snippet: Gold Terra Resource (TSX-V: YGT) reported the first six sonic drill results from historical tailings at the Con Mine in Yellowknife, Northwest Territories, confirming gold mineralization averaging 0.8 g/t Au over up to 18 metres — with a peak interval of 3.75 g/t Au. The Con Mine was one of Canada's largest historic gold producers and its tailings represent a potential low-capital reprocessing opportunity. With tailings operations requiring less capital than conventional mining, confirming grade continuity from material untouched for over 30 years is a meaningful first step toward resource classification.

headline: SILVER BOW MINING ENTERS NASDAQ JUNIOR SILVER MINERS INDEX — Butte Underground Exploration Resumes After 30-Year District Dormancy
snippet: Silver Bow Mining joined the Nasdaq Junior Silver Miners Index on November 23, adding institutional indexation visibility to a company that recently began the first underground exploration drilling in the Butte silver district in over three decades — testing extensions to its 170 Moz AgEq Inferred Mineral Resource at the Rainbow Decline. Index inclusion typically improves liquidity and forces passive fund allocations, a meaningful catalyst for small-cap silver explorers with limited institutional following, especially at a moment when silver is trading 60% below its 2026 high.

headline: USAGOLD NOV 23: GOLD SETTLES 2.5% HIGHER AT $3,634 — Half-Point Fed Hike Bets Fade as Dollar Rally Finally Stalls; Silver Up 3.6%
snippet: USAGold's November 23 daily metals report frames gold's 2.5% recovery to $3,634 as a direct response to fading bets on a 50-basis-point December Federal Reserve rate hike — a scenario the market had been pricing at near-certainty last week. Silver outperformed at +3.6%, recovering from a 15% weekly collapse. The report notes the dollar rally has stalled at 19-month highs rather than extending, providing the technical opening for the first meaningful precious metals recovery since the AI-driven forced liquidation began on November 17.

headline: GOLD MINERS AT CHEAPEST VALUATIONS IN YEARS DESPITE RECORD Q3 EARNINGS — GDXJ Hits Most Oversold Reading in 4 Years
snippet: An Investing.com analysis argues that gold mining stocks have entered historically cheap valuation territory despite the sector just delivering one of its strongest-ever quarterly earnings reports — a disconnect driven by gold's 9% weekly correction and the GDXJ small-cap miner ETF touching its most oversold reading in four years. The piece flags a critical risk: if gold averages near current levels through December, Q4 2026 could be the first negative-average-gold-price quarter since Q4 2022, creating genuine fundamental uncertainty that makes the cheap valuation case conditional on the gold price holding.

headline: COMEX COPPER CONFIRMED IN BEAR MARKET — 20.4% BELOW SEPTEMBER RECORD AS NVIDIA AI DEAL PAUSE REMOVES DEMAND TIMELINE CERTAINTY
snippet: COMEX copper settled 20.4% below its September 2026 record of $6.889/lb after seven straight losing sessions, confirming a technical bear market as the Nvidia AI deal pause removed near-term demand timeline certainty. Discovery Alert distinguishes between the financial-market bear market price and physical reality: Chinese smelters continued paying record import premiums of $360-500/tonne, suggesting the futures selloff was leveraged position liquidation rather than collapsing end-user demand. With Nvidia's CEO now confirmed returning, the analysis asks whether the AI copper demand timeline has been deferred or destroyed.

headline: URANIUM SUPPLY SHORTFALL: CAN CAMECO, NEXGEN AND DENISON BRIDGE THE GAP? — Spot $90/lb, Long-Term Contracts at Record $99, Equities Down 31% YTD
snippet: Discovery Alert examines whether the three most-followed Canadian uranium developers — Cameco (CCJ), NexGen Energy and Denison Mines — can deliver production volumes needed to cover global supply shortfalls given the current pricing signals: spot at $90/lb and TradeTech long-term at a nominal record $99/lb, yet URNM equity ETF down 31% year-to-date. The analysis identifies the core paradox: utilities are contracting at record long-term prices, Cameco's Q3 realized price was approximately $65.8/lb against $90/lb spot, and production expansions are running behind schedule — an earnings upgrade cycle not yet priced into depressed equities.

headline: 5 GOLD MINERS WORTH WATCHING AFTER THE WORST WEEK OF 2026 — Relative Strength and Balance Sheet Screen Identifies Recovery Candidates
snippet: Canadian Mining Report ran a relative-strength and balance-sheet screen across senior and mid-tier gold miners following the worst weekly selloff of 2026, identifying five names that held up better than the sector and carry the financial resilience to weather further weakness. With GDXJ down more than 30% from its August peak and gold at 14-month lows, the analysis provides a framework for distinguishing distressed names from fundamentally discounted ones — a distinction that becomes critical when margin-call selling creates uniform drawdowns regardless of company quality.
